project_type: AWS Lambda Python application. Reference sample is SNS->SQS->Lambda->DynamoDB+Bedrock->external RPA. We are adding a LangGraph+FastAPI agent Lambda alongside the reference files.
build_system: No build tool / packaging config exists. Lambda layer is built manually: pip install -r requirements.txt -t python/ ; zip -r layer.zip python. boto3 is runtime-bundled and must NOT be in the layer (pin only for local/tests). The actual Lambda deployment zip contains just the .py files + test_page.html; third-party deps ship as a layer.
test_framework: None exists yet. Add pytest + mocking (moto for DynamoDB, unittest.mock for Bedrock/requests/socialmessaging). Create pytest.ini/conftest.py and a tests/ dir. All tests run fully offline.
build_command: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt   (into a Python 3.12 venv)
verification_instructions: 1) Create a clean Python 3.12 venv and `pip install -r requirements.txt`. 2) Import check: `python -c "import app, agent, checkpointer, data, whatsapp"`. 3) `python -m pytest -q` runs the offline suite green: data (moto), checkpointer round-trip, agent five HITL scenarios (unauthorized-reject, authorized-proceed, interrupt-before-HTTP-no-POST, resume-triggers-POST+mapping-write, callback-produces-message+history-write), FastAPI TestClient GET / and POST /ask with Bedrock/DynamoDB mocked, and dispatcher routing an SQS event to the SQS path. Grep is NOT verification.
environment_constraints: boto3 is bundled in the AWS Lambda Python 3.12 runtime; do not add it to the layer. No AWS credentials/network in tests: mock Bedrock (ChatBedrockConverse), DynamoDB, requests (order API), and the socialmessaging client. Never hardcode model ids, table names, endpoints, or keys; all come from env vars. The HTML page is opened from file:// so the Function URL needs permissive CORS.
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING/.kiro steering files exist in the repo (only the sample README.md). Hard rule from the task: DO NOT modify or delete handler.py or whatsapp_lambda.py — they are reference. Reuse whatsapp_lambda.py helpers verbatim (import them). All config via env vars, no hardcoded secrets. Target Python 3.12.
key_patterns: whatsapp_lambda.py defines the proven outbound send: send_whatsapp_message(destination, text) uses boto3 client('socialmessaging'), API send_whatsapp_message(originationPhoneNumberId=WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, metaApiVersion=META_API_VERSION, message=json.dumps({messaging_product:'whatsapp', recipient_type:'individual', to, type:'text', text:{body}})). It also has extract_webhook_data(sqs_record), extract_text_messages(webhook)->[{sender,message_id,text}], normalize_destination(phone). handler.py shows the SQS batch pattern: iterate event['Records'], isolate per-record failures, return {'batchItemFailures':[{'itemIdentifier':messageId}]}, and a DynamoDB turn-append pattern with TTL expires_at. Both are reference; the new SQS path mirrors handler.py's batch shape but reuses whatsapp_lambda's extractors.

whatsapp_lambda.py (READ ONLY reference: import send_whatsapp_message, extract_webhook_data, extract_text_messages, normalize_destination)

env_vars.BEDROCK_MODEL_ID: Bedrock model/inference-profile id for ChatBedrockConverse (default a Claude inference-profile id)
env_vars.CHAT_HISTORY_TABLE_NAME: conversation turns, PK conversation_id (S), SK sk (S)
env_vars.CHECKPOINTER_TABLE_NAME: LangGraph checkpointer, PK pk (S), SK sk (S), TTL on expires_at
env_vars.ORDER_API_KEY: optional bearer/api key for the order endpoint
env_vars.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID: origination phone number id for socialmessaging send (send gated on presence)
